title: Pricing SKU, quota enforcement modes, and overage playbook
creator: Ava Martínez
description:
Purpose: Define SKU-level entitlements, quota types (rate limits vs monthly quotas), enforcement modes (soft-limit warnings, hard-blocking, grace/overage), and the billing-side acceptance criteria for Redwood’s updated pricing plans.

Background: We are launching a revised pricing model that introduces per-SKU entitlements (tokens, embeddings, realtime-connections), tiered monthly quotas, and optional overage billing. The Console and API must surface quota state, warnings, and provide deterministic behavior for enforcement. Billing must ingest metering events and produce accurate invoices with overage line items. This ticket captures product requirements, success criteria, edge cases, migration considerations, and acceptance tests for the billing integration and UI notifications.
scope: In scope: SKU definitions, quota types, enforcement rules, warning/notification UX, metering event schema, billing reconciliation rules, migration path for existing customers. Out of scope: pricing numbers/discount negotiations, tax handling, third-party marketplace billing flows (handled separately).
requirements: Define SKUs: text-generation-tokens, chat-turns, embedding-units, realtime-connections, dedicated-throughput-hours
Support two quota dimensions: rate_limit (requests/sec or tokens/sec) and monthly_quota (units per billing period)
Three enforcement modes configurable per plan and per SKU: soft (warn), hard (deny), overage (allow + bill)
Soft-mode: send progressive warnings at 80%, 95% of quota and allow requests; include exponential backoff recommendations in response headers
Hard-mode: return standardized 429 with quota code and 'retry-after' header when limit exceeded
Overage-mode: allow requests beyond quota, record overage units to metering stream, cap overage by plan-specific max_overage if configured
Console: per-customer dashboard showing current usage, predicted spend, next-billing-period reset date, and action links to upgrade or set alerts
API: include 'x-redwood-quota-remaining', 'x-redwood-quota-reset', and 'x-redwood-plan-entitlement' headers on responses
Billing: meter events must be idempotent, time-windowed, and include SKU, customer_id, unit_count, usage_timestamp, request_id
Reconciliation: billing must support retroactive corrections for up to 90 days with explanation logs and audit trail
Migration: existing customers on legacy unlimited token plans must be mapped to an appropriate SKU with grace periods and explicit opt-in to overage billing
Telemetry: create alerts for anomalous usage (>= 3x baseline) and for 10+ customers hitting overage in a 24-hour window
Legal/compliance: overage waiver or dispute process documented and surfaced to CS and Billing teams
constraints: Metering pipeline has 5s expected lag to billing ingestion; acceptance criteria should allow for eventual consistency where appropriate
Rate-limit decisions must be enforced at the edge runtime for latency reasons; quota syncs to control plane may be eventual
Any hard-blocking behavior must degrade gracefully for private deployments (VPC) where control-plane communication may be restricted
Overage caps cannot exceed the customer's maximum_commit value stored in contract metadata without explicit approval
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: For a test customer on soft enforcement, when usage crosses 80% and 95% of monthly_quota, the Console shows two warnings and API responses contain 'x-redwood-quota-remaining' and an 'X-Redwood-Warning' header; no requests are rejected

AC-2: For a test customer on hard enforcement, when exceeding rate_limit or monthly_quota, the runtime returns 429 responses with a standardized JSON body containing 'error.code': 'quota_exceeded' and 'retry_after' seconds; Console shows blocked request counter

AC-3: For a test customer on overage enforcement with no max_overage, requests beyond quota succeed and billing receives idempotent metering events labeled as 'overage' with unit_count accurate to within +/-1% on aggregate across 1M tokens

AC-4: Billing generates a preview invoice in the Console that includes overage line items and predicted charges for next period when called via 'Generate invoice preview' with sample rates; preview math matches metering aggregation for a 30-day sample dataset

AC-5: Migration path: three legacy customers moved to new SKU mapping receive a 60-day free grace buffer; their Console shows 'migration_grace_period' and they are not billed for overage during the buffer
AC-6: Edge: If billing ingestion is delayed >120s, the Console shows 'usage delayed' indicator; no hard-blocking occurs solely because of delayed ingestion
AC-7: Security: Overages and billing-sensitive events are logged to audit with immutable IDs; test case demonstrates a 90-day correction logged and attached to invoice metadata

AC-8: Private deployment behavior: For a simulated VPC customer with control-plane disconnects, local enforcement honors hard-rate limits for 5 minutes using last-known quota state and then transitions to soft warnings
AC-9: Observability: SLO for quota header correctness is 99.9% per day; automated smoke test verifies headers on 1000 sample calls
ui_requirements: Console must expose an 'Entitlements' tab per customer showing SKU rows, current_period_usage, quota, enforcement_mode, and upgrade action
Warning banners that are dismissible with reason capture (e.g., 'critical test run') must be available to org-admins
Invoice preview UI must show line-by-line SKU counts, unit price, and total cost with a 'Download CSV' option
Notifications: email + in-console with configurable thresholds (80/90/100%). Defaults are 80% and 95%
API error payload samples must be documented in the developer docs and linked from the Console when a customer clicks 'Why was I blocked?'
metering_schema: Flat text: meter_event_v1 => fields: customer_id, sku, unit_count, usage_timestamp (ISO8601), request_id (uuid), plan_id, enforcement_mode, is_overage (true/false as string), source_route, model_name
migration_plan: Phase 1 (30 days): Create SKU mappings and internal-only migration preview for legacy accounts
Phase 2 (30 days): Notify customers with recommended mappings and auto-schedule migration with opt-out
Phase 3 (60 days): Execute migration with 60-day grace period for billing; CS playbook ready for disputes
Rollback: Provide toggle to revert mapping per-customer for 14 days post-migration.
security_and_compliance_notes: All metering events must be signed with a service token before entering the billing pipeline
Audit logs for billing adjustments retained for minimum 7 years per finance request
Security review required for invoice preview and overage flows due to PHI risk in enterprise SKUs
open_questions: Should we support per-route quotas (e.g., embeddings separate from text tokens) by default or behind a flag?
What is the default max_overage for Free and Starter plans? Needs legal/finance signoff
How should credits (promotional or trial) interact with overage calculations — consumed first or last?
Exact content and cadence for migration notifications to enterprise customers (CS vs automated emails)
